latest.name: Elicit — AI Scientific Research Assistant
latest.category: General-purpose, research, reasoning and multimodal AI
latest.short_verdict: Elicit is a specialist academic-research assistant for finding papers, summarizing studies, asking questions across research literature, and producing cited reports. Its Basic plan is genuinely free, with unlimited paper search across the vendor-listed 138M+ corpus, unlimited summaries and paper chat; Research Agent and Report usage is limited by an undisclosed monthly pool. Useful for early evidence discovery, but not a replacement for exhaustive database searches or human verification.
latest.what_it_does: Elicit uses semantic search and language models to find relevant academic papers, summarize them, answer questions using paper content, extract structured information, and create cited research reports. Its Research Agent can also use the wider web and uploaded research materials; official help says a session can include up to 100 uploaded resources totaling up to 10GB. The official site lists a corpus of more than 138 million academic papers and 545,000 clinical trials, although the free Basic pricing card specifically promises paper search, not unlimited clinical-trial search. The full Systematic Review workflow is reserved for Pro, Scale and Enterprise plans.
latest.why_try_it: It is worth trying when a question needs evidence from academic papers rather than a generic chatbot answer. The free tier lets users search the paper corpus, summarize papers and chat with papers while viewing sources, which can help build an initial reading list or compare findings. Treat it as a discovery and first-pass synthesis assistant, then open the cited papers and verify important claims yourself.
latest.free_tier: Basic costs $0. The official pricing page lists unlimited search across more than 138 million papers, unlimited summaries, unlimited chat with papers with full-text access, source viewing for answers, and Zotero import. Research Agent sessions and Research Reports are available on all plans but are subject to a limited monthly usage pool. Elicit does not publish a numeric Basic-plan allowance. The usage pool is shared across covered workflows, varies with task size and complexity, resets monthly, and unused usage does not roll over.
latest.limits: The exact monthly Basic usage amount for Research Agent and Reports is not published. Usage is complexity-based rather than a fixed number of actions; after the included usage is exhausted, the Research Agent is restricted to Find Papers use cases until the next monthly reset. Systematic Review workflows are Pro or higher. Paper coverage can be incomplete: when Elicit cannot access a paper PDF, extraction may rely on the abstract only. Independent research has found useful extraction performance in some small studies but also substantial recall gaps in literature search, so it should supplement—not replace—conventional database searches and human review. No official Elicit Android app was verified. The linked Privacy Policy and general Terms currently display a 2023 update date; review current terms before uploading confidential or client material.
latest.signup_pakistan: The Elicit Authorized User Terms last updated 2025-08-25 name embargoed jurisdictions (including Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea, DNR and LNR) but do not name Pakistan. This is not a guarantee of access: Pakistan-based registration and service use were not independently tested, and acceptance of Pakistani cards or other payment methods was not verified. The free Basic plan is listed at $0, so paid checkout is not needed to try its free features.
latest.quality_evidence: Vendor claims: Elicit's current homepage says it is trusted by over 5 million researchers and searches more than 138 million papers plus 545,000 clinical trials; these are vendor-reported figures, not independently audited. Independent evidence is mixed and task-specific: a 2025 proof-of-concept study comparing 43 studies and 602 data points reported 81.4% extraction accuracy for Elicit versus 86.7% for human reviewers, with no statistically significant difference. A separate 2025 study across 30 articles reported 92% precision, recall and F1 for Elicit data extraction but found four confabulations. In contrast, a 2025 four-case study of literature searching reported average sensitivity of 39.5% for Elicit versus 94.5% for the original review searches, concluding it should be supplementary rather than a replacement. Anecdotal community feedback: a May 2026 Reddit comparison rated Elicit 3/5, praising paper organization and structured insights but describing the workflow as somewhat rigid; this is an individual opinion, not a benchmark. No hands-on test was performed for this report.
latest.android_status: No official Android app published by Elicit Research, PBC was verified on Google Play. A similarly named listing, “Elicit AI Research,” is published by Yeteamapps and describes a general study/essay app; it is not the Elicit academic-research service and should not be treated as official. The Elicit website can be opened in a mobile browser, but a native official Android app was not verified.
